title: The Lavalle House in Pensacola, Florida, built in 1805 and restored - NewsBreak
text: The historic Lavalle House at 203 East Church Street in Pensacola, Florida (Escambia County) was built in 1805. It wa added to the U.S. National Register of Historic Places on March 11, 1971. It's also part of the Historic Pensacola Village. This house is one of the few that remain from Spanish Florida in Pensacola. The house was relocated in 1969 from 111 West Government Street to its current location by the Historic Pensacola Preservation Board so it wouldn't be demolished. The builder and property owner was Carlos, or Charles, Lavalle. From 1803 to 1815, he owned the property. At the time of his death in 1854, he owned numerous properties. Lavalle was a landowner, builder, and brick mason. He rented houses and invested in property. He also built houses which he might have sold for profit. In 1807, his partner, Marianna Bonifay, bought a brickyard by Escambia Bay. Accoring to Bonifay family information , Marianna and Carlos (or Charles) bought property, built homes, and sold them. They started a successful brickyard. The information also indicates that Carlos fathered children with Marianna: Josefa Maria, Julian, Andres Antonio, and Josefa Candalaria born between around 1798 and 1806. Lavelle owned his house for 12 years. He sold his house, property, and furnishings. There aren't many structures from 1781-1821, which was the Spanish period of occupation. The house is noted as being a good example of the French Creole architectural style . The main floor of the original house had four rooms on the main floor an a large loft that was unfinished. The house contains artifacts from the 1700s and 1800s. This house is part of the Historic House Tour. Visit here for information . Thanks for reading and sharing.
